title: Free roads
statement:
A country has n towns (1..n) and m two-way roads. Road i joins towns ui and vi and costs wi to travel. You hold k vouchers; each voucher lets you travel one road for free (a voucher is used up after one road). Find the minimum cost to travel from town 1 to town n.
Input: the first line holds n, m and k (2 <= n <= 10000, 1 <= m <= 30000, 0 <= k <= 10). Each of the next m lines holds ui vi wi (1 <= ui, vi <= n, ui != vi, 1 <= wi <= 1000000). There may be several roads between the same two towns.
Output: a single integer, the minimum cost, or -1 if town n cannot be reached from town 1.
Trying every choice of free roads, or a Dijkstra without a priority queue, is too slow for the largest tests.

Example
Input:
4 4 1
1 2 10
2 4 10
1 3 1
3 4 100
Output:
1
(Go 1 -> 3 paying 1, then use the voucher on the road 3 -> 4.)
